body: In Theory-of-Mind (ToM) reasoning, large language models may correctly infer the agent's mental state but fail to use that inference when predicting or judging the agent's subsequent actions. In this work, we investigate whether explicitly connecting perception, belief, and action with rules improves ToM reasoning. We generate concise if--then rules that express relations between perception to action and use Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to train Qwen2.5 and Llama3 models across four ToM benchmarks. GRPO with rule generation outperforms prompting, supervised fine-tuning, and think reasoning. Moreover, rules generated by larger models (≥3B) provide transferable knowledge that improves downstream performance of GPT-4o-mini. These findings suggest that explicit rules help models bridge the reasoning gap in ToM and support knowledge transfer across models.
summaryZh: 通过心理理论推理的强化学习学习对动作规则的感知。在心理理论（ToM）推理中，大型语言模型可能会正确推断智能体的心理状态，但在预测或判断智能体后续动作时无法使用该推理。在这项工作中，我们研究了将感知、信念和行动与规则明确联系起来是否可以改善 ToM 推理。
